dedupe_keys.name: uganda service availability and readiness assessment sara 2013 analytic file essential medicines for non communicable diseases in 196 facilities

description: This analytic file takes Uganda's 2013 Service Availability and Readiness Assessment, the World Health Organization's standard survey of whether health facilities are equipped to provide services, and extracts what 196 facilities had on hand to treat non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and hypertension. The producers are Mari Armstrong-Hough of the Yale School of Public Health and co-authors including staff of Uganda's Ministry of Health. Coverage is national, with facilities of all types and managing authorities. Each row gives the number of essential medicines available and facility characteristics: basic amenities such as power and water, equipment, region, facility type, public or private management, diagnostic capacity and HIV services. The workbook, with a variable list, is available as a free download from Dryad, mirrored on Zenodo, under the CC0 dedication. Caveats: a 2013 snapshot, facilities are not geolocated in the file, and only the variables used in the regression are included, not the full survey. Simulation uses: representing facility readiness and medicine availability, including links to power and water amenities, in health system capacity models, and identifying regions where disruption would hit already weak facilities. Related records: the Mtwara neonatal care unit survey (data-tanzania-mtwara-neonatal-care-units) is a similar facility assessment, and healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) gives facility locations.
